behavioral_observations.observation: Fouls committed against Real Madrid (i.e. fouls Real Madrid draw) average 14.29/match long-run, rising sharply to 18.4/match in the last 5. Yellow cards shown to Real Madrid's opponents rose from 2.14 (long-run) to 3.4 (last 5).

Athletic Club commit 12.67 fouls/match long-run (11.8 last 5) and receive 2.21 yellow cards/match long-run (2.0 last 5). Their fouls committed are above Real Madrid's long-run average of 9.57 fouls committed.

final_candidate.falsifiable_question: When Athletic Club play at home against opponents whose defensive/discipline profile is similar to Real Madrid's, do Athletic's fouls_for and yellow_cards_for differ from their overall home baseline?
final_candidate.falsifier: If Athletic's fouls_for and yellow_cards_for against similar-profile opponents are not systematically different from their overall home baseline, the mechanism is unsupported.
final_candidate.football_mechanism: A possession-dominant side that draws fouls frequently (Real Madrid) meeting a physically active pressing side (Athletic) that commits fouls at above-average rates creates a structural interaction: Athletic's pressing style may generate more fouls against Real Madrid than against lower-quality opponents, and Real Madrid's movement in tight spaces draws fouls from opponents who cannot win the ball cleanly. This tests whether Athletic's foul rate is elevated when facing opponents with Real Madrid's profile.

self_critique.notes: The mechanism requires two characteristics together: Athletic's pressing foul rate AND Real Madrid's foul-drawing profile. This is a genuine interaction, not a single-metric observation.

final_candidate.similar_opponent_rationale: Real Madrid's profile — low goals conceded, low shots on target conceded, low fouls committed — identifies a specific type of technically proficient, disciplined opponent. Athletic's foul and card behaviour against such opponents tests whether their pressing style generates more discipline events against this type.
final_candidate.subject: TEAM_B

incremental_structure: Subject is TEAM_B (Real Madrid) as the OPPONENT whose foul-drawing profile defines the cohort, while TEAM_A (Athletic Club) is the measured subject for fouls_for/yellow_cards_for
The mechanism requires a JOINT interaction: Athletic's pressing foul-rate AND Real Madrid's foul-drawing profile together, not either characteristic alone
The falsifiable question is directed at Athletic's (TEAM_A/home side) discipline output against a similar-profile opponent cohort, not the away team's concession rate
opponent_profile axis is implicitly defined by Real Madrid's low-foul-committed, high-foul-drawn, technically proficient profile — a cross-team interaction condition absent from all three generics
response.reason: All three generic structures measure the AWAY team's discipline concessions (fouls/yellow_cards AGAINST the away team) against a similar-opponent cohort at home. Candidate C4 inverts the measurement axis: it measures TEAM_B's (Real Madrid's) fouls drawn (AGAINST perspective on TEAM_B) as the cohort-defining characteristic, and then asks whether TEAM_A's (Athletic Club's, the home side's) foul-committing and card-receiving behaviour is elevated when facing opponents with Real Madrid's foul-drawing profile. The subject of measurement is the HOME team's discipline output, not the away team's concession rate. Additionally, the mechanism is a two-characteristic interaction — Athletic's pressing style co-occurring with Real Madrid's foul-drawing tendency — which is structurally absent from all three generics. The window (W10) and venue condition (HOME) are shared, but the subject identity, measurement direction, and interaction requirement are all distinct. KEEP is warranted.
